g.title: cluster_sim
g.text: Simulator — owns the clock, the jobs, and the backlog

g.title: cluster_hw
g.text: Cluster — owns machines only, never sees a Job

g.title: cluster_sched
g.text: sched — two independent halves of one decision

g.title: cluster_trace
g.text: TraceWriter — optional JSONL log, observes and owns nothing

g.title: cluster_after
g.text: After run() returns — offline, reads jobs_ only

g.title: wgen
g.text: Poisson arrival; a second pass draws

g.title: sealed
g.text: Fixed before the clock starts, so it
cannot depend on a scheduling decision.

g.title: jobs
g.text: the full record, indexed by JobId

g.title: run
g.text: seed the queue, then pop until empty.

g.title: run->queue
g.text: When the queue drains, one SimEnd

g.title: simend
g.text: the run's upper limit: closes the

g.title: trace
g.text: job_spec(Job) the workload, once, before t = 0
write(Event) every event, in pop order

g.title: drain
g.text: phase 1 strict FIFO from the head
phase 2 whatever may jump a blocked head

g.title: running
g.text: on a node right now. Projected into
RunningJob so a policy can see finish

g.title: qpol
g.text: fifo: never. backfill: EASY, admits a job
predicted to finish before the head's

g.title: sched
g.text: span is const: a policy cannot mutate

g.title: metrics
g.text: censored jobs counted, never silently dropped
percentiles() → p50 / p95 / p99 (reorders its input)
